title: Room and connection contracts
description: The room (place) definition kind and its exits (21 §5 Place/Room, Connection; 05 §17; 00 §4.1, §4.10; 00a §2, §12), owned by movement (capability_registry.json). R5 slice 1: what look and move need; slice 2: inspectable details; slice 3: description variants. Tags and barriers join with their capabilities as optional fields, which keep the loka-cartridge-v2 tag (CompiledCartridge compatibility rule); contents are derived from containment (03 §23), not stored in the room.

Alias.description: A word or phrase a player types to name a detail (21 §6 aliases; 04 §18 aliases) or, for an ActionRecipe, the action (its verb, the first words typed): lowercase letters and digits, the words of a phrase joined by _ (the player's `mooring post` is compared as mooring_post; kernel/ts/src/target.ts gives the normalization). At most 64 characters.

Connection.description: One directed exit to another room of the same cartridge (21 §5 Connection; 05 §17). Its identity is its room and direction. barrier, optional (barrier@1), names the Barrier whose one shared state the exit passes through (21 §5 Barrier; 05 §25 coherent connections): move through it is refused while it is closed (exit_closed) or locked (exit_locked); an exit without one means what it always meant. A reciprocal exit is authored in the destination room (00a §2); the two faces of one door name the same barrier: an exit and each exit of its destination back to its room name the same barrier or none (BARRIER_MISMATCH).

InspectableDetail.description: A lightweight keyed detail of a room (21 §6 InspectableDetail): the aliases a player can name it by, the first of which also names it when a lookup is ambiguous, and its description text key (05 §18). Not a RuntimeEntity: a fresh world gives it a target id only (numeric profile, Initial world ids). Two details of one room may share an alias (an ambiguous lookup lists both, 04 §18), but the first alias must be the detail's own and in the form a lookup produces (no empty word, not starting with at, the, a or an), or the player could not pick it by name (UNREACHABLE_DETAIL). Its variants (DescriptionVariant) select other prose by condition. Owned by inspectable_detail (a cartridge with details requires it). R5 freezes this v1 shape (14 §R5): perception, reveal facts and contextual actions join as optional fields.

RoomDefinition.description: A navigable place (21 §5 Place/Room): its key, its title and description text keys (05 §18; resolved in the cartridge text catalog), and its exits by compass direction, the six-way compass of 00 §4.10 (a direction without an exit is absent), optionally its inspectable details by key, at most 64, its description variants (DescriptionVariant) and its contributions to the ActionSet of an actor in it, applied in order (action.schema.json ActionContribution; R5 S5, optional). Custom named connections (05 §17) join later as a separate optional field.

DescriptionVariant.description: Prose selected by a condition (21 §6 DescriptionVariant; 00a §12): description replaces the base description key when the condition holds for the actor over committed state (policy.schema.json VersionedPolicy; the evaluator is pure, 06 §21). A room's or detail's variants are tried in list order and the first whose condition holds is shown; when none holds, the base description is. Variants are derived, never a mutated description (21 §6). Owned by description_variant (a cartridge with one requires it); its condition's ops by their owners.

BarrierState.description: A barrier's state (21 §5 Barrier: open/closed, locked/unlocked): open, closed (and unlocked) or locked (and closed); a lock needs a closed door, so an open locked barrier does not exist. The legal transitions (04 §5.3 'Lifecycle transition') are closed to open (open), open to closed (close), closed to locked (lock) and locked to closed (unlock); delta.schema.json barrier.transition.

BarrierDefinition.description: Shared mutable state for one logical door or gate (21 §5 Barrier), owned by barrier@1 (a cartridge with one requires it), keyed in CompiledCartridge.barriers by DefinitionRefString of kind barrier and named by the exits that pass through it (Connection.barrier): its key; keywords, the Alias words a player names it by after open, close, lock or unlock (the direction of its exit names it too); short, the text key of its short description ("the oak door"); initial, its state in a fresh world (BarrierState); and optionally key_item, the item whose holder may lock and unlock it (has_item: held directly or inside containers the holder holds). Without key_item no one can lock or unlock it. Damaged/repaired and blocked states join as optional fields.
